main_text.l: Huc facit etiam Psalmus Dauidis 128. qui sic
incipit: Beatus quicunq; timet Dominum,
qui ambulat in viis eius,&c.
3 Porrò si beatus est vir, qui habet vxo-
rem bonam & strenuam, quàm beati sunt &
vir & mulier, quorum sponsus & maritus est
optimus ille & maximus, clementissimus &
potentissimus rex, idem & speciosissimus in-
ter filios hominum Iesus Christus, Dei &
Mariæ filius: de quo Paulus 2. Corinth. 11.
Adiunxi vos vni viro, &c. qui & agnus Dei,
& leo de tribu Iuda recte dicitur, propter su-
am mansuetudinem & fortitudinem, Ioan.1.
Apoc. 5. Hic est illa sapientia, de qua Sap.8
Hanc amaui & exquisiui à iuuentute mea,&c

page.notes: Greek phrase at the start of the Siracid citation ("ἐν [?]μερίδι φοβουμένων κύριον δοθήσεται") is only partly legible at this resolution; the first word and the middle word are doubtful. German black-letter line in parentheses: the word after "mans" is doubtful (ö), and the hyphen at the line end is uncertain. Long s is printed as f throughout and is transcribed as s. Small dots in the right margin and the dot below the last line are specks, not text. The decorative mark at bottom left is not text.
